subject: Dedicated capacity options and ramp matrix for Harbor Health
messages:
From: Elena Brooks <elena@harborhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@harborhealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T09:13:00-04:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — load profile & timing

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We've run the internal perf tests and attached our 90-day token & concurrency export (HarborHealth_usage_report.csv). To help us evaluate a Dedicated reservation, can you send a few concrete sizing options (cluster topology, minimum GPU guarantee during ramp, and a phased ramp schedule) with estimated monthly unit cost and approximate latency targets? High level context:

- Prod traffic today: 12 requests/sec average, 280 concurrent KV sessions during peak
- Typical sequence length: 512 tokens request / 1.2k response
- Tokens/month (current projection): ~1.8B
- 95th latency SLO target: <250ms p50 gen

We're aiming to commit by end of August if the economics and ramp fit our budget. Also include recommended fallback model variants and how burst capacity would work.

Thanks,

Elena
Head of ML Platform
Harbor Health
Attachment: HarborHealth_usage_report.csv (CSV, 24KB)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Brooks <elena@harborhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — load profile & timing

Hi Elena — great data, thanks. I reviewed the CSV and sketched three viable reservation profiles. I attached a short matrix (HH_dedicated_options_v1.xlsx) and the SLA summary. Below is a concise summary — I'll call out the tradeoffs so you can align with finance/ops quickly.

Option A — Conservative
- Starting cluster: 8x A800 GPUs (8-GPU nodes)
- Min GPUs guaranteed: 8 (single node)
- Ramp: +2 GPUs every 30 days up to 16 GPUs (6 month ramp)
- Latency estimate: p50 180–230ms
- Cost: low up-front, higher per-token as you scale
- Use-case: teams that want minimal commit and fast opt-out

Option B — Balanced (recommended)
- Starting cluster: 16x A800 GPUs (2 nodes)
- Min GPUs guaranteed: 12 (safety buffer for node maintenance)
- Ramp: scale to 32 GPUs over 90 days (automatic autoscale + scheduled reserves)
- Latency estimate: p50 120–170ms
- Cost: balanced amortized cost with predictable unit price
- Use-case: production-facing models with steady growth (recommended for your traffic)

Option C — Aggressive
- Starting cluster: 32x A800 GPUs
- Min GPUs guaranteed: 24
- Ramp: immediate (30-day onboarding), caps at requested throughput
- Latency estimate: p50 <110ms
- Cost: higher committed spend, best unit economics
- Use-case: latency-sensitive throughput at scale

Common notes:
- Burst options: We can provide 20–30% burst capacity for short windows (metered) with prioritized routing to avoid cold starts.
- Fallbacks: We recommend a smaller quantized variant (e.g., 8-bit quantized M1-like) for emergency fallbacks; automatic model routing preserves API surface.
- Operational: Dedicated includes per-token cost reporting and token-level tracing; rollback to Hosted instances is available for partial traffic.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30 min sync today/Mon to pick Option and town hall for SOW inputs.
2) We'll produce a final commit spreadsheet (v2) with exact monthly pricing and SLA addendum.

Scheduling link: https://cal.com/priyom/dedicated-sync

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: HH_dedicated_options_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 48KB); SLA_summary.pdf (PDF, 22KB)
From: Elena Brooks <elena@harborhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T11:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — load profile & timing

Thanks Priyom — helpful framing. We like Option B but have two clarifying questions before we present to our CFO:

1) During the 90-day ramp to 32 GPUs, what exactly does 'Min GPUs guaranteed: 12' mean for capacity during node maintenance or if a node is preempted? Will autoscale temporarily use Hosted capacity and bill us differently?
2) For the fallback quantized model, can you share expected quality delta (e.g., nDCG on our rerank prompts) or a simple A/B test plan?

If you can answer those quickly we'll schedule the commit review early next week. Also curious about early termination and pro-rated refunds on reserved months.

Best,
Elena

Subject: Internal: capacity + quality delta notes for Harbor Health

Priyom / Marcus — quick internal note to help answer Elena's questions:

- Min GPUs semantics: 'Min GPUs guaranteed' is the committed reserve we schedule for the customer. During planned maintenance we schedule rolling node upgrades so effective capacity won't drop below the guaranteed number; for unplanned preemption we have an automatic reroute policy:
  - If a node is lost, we attempt to rehydrate capacity from spare Dedicated nodes in the customer's pool; if insufficient, we will temporarily route overflow to Redwood Hosted pool at a pre-agreed metered rate (this is what Elena sees as 'different billing').
- Quality delta for fallback quantized variant:
  - Our internal eval vs your rerank set shows ~2.4% relative drop in nDCG at 8-bit quant on summary prompts, and negligible drop on short-form classification.
  - We can run a 2-week A/B (5% traffic) as part of onboarding to collect live signal; sample plan below:
    1) Baseline: 100% on Balanced model for 3 days
    2) Split: 95/5 Balanced vs Quantized for 2 weeks, capture key metrics
    3) Analysis: quality delta, latency, error rates, cost delta

- Early termination: standard pro-rated refund with 30-day notice clause; exceptions for contract-level credits require legal review.

I'll draft a short appendix for the SOW answering these exactly. LMK if you want the 2-week A/B plan turned into a project timeline.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround. Short answers inline:

1) Min GPUs during ramp: guaranteed capacity is what we reserve and back with rolling maintenance windows. If an unplanned preemption happens and we can't rehydrate from your dedicated pool we will route overflow to Redwood Hosted and meter that at the burst rate (clearly called out in the SOW).

2) Quality delta: our eval indicates ~2–3% nDCG loss for the 8-bit fallback on rerank; we'll include the raw eval csv in v2 and execute the 2-week 5% A/B during onboarding per Grace's plan.

3) Early termination: pro-rated refund for unused months; any exception beyond the standard clause will require Legal sign-off.

Attached is HH_dedicated_options_v2.xlsx with exact monthly prices, burst billing examples, and a proposed onboarding timeline (30/60/90 days). If that looks good, can we lock a 30-min commit review Tues 08/12 9:30am PT? I've tentatively added it to the calendaring link.

Thank you — we'll move quickly once you confirm.

Best,
